content: In the Prologue Melvin-Koushki calls the Mafāḥiṣ's opening declaration 'Letters are Moons', whose quranic miraculous splitting (shaqq-i qamar) is the splitting of the Pen that writes the world; in a footnote he adds that for Ibn Turka the continuum from letter-cutting (the cut letters, muqaṭṭaʿāt, opening 29 suras) to moon-splitting to ʿAlī as Pythagoras redivivus and inventor of letter science 'could not be more patent'.
